summary: B is preferable because it confines replayability changes to v1 file uploads and centralizes request construction, whereas A introduces an expressly out-of-scope, SDK-wide RawClient buffering policy. Neither patch fully follows the contract.
reasons: B keeps the retry fix within FilesService; A changes RawClient.Do so every io.Reader across the SDK is eagerly buffered unless WithNoRetry is set.
B shares option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data checks through add; A duplicates the existing Add implementation inside Upload.
B's retry test verifies multipart field name, filename, and content on both attempts using an os.File source.
A has stronger validation and source-error tests, but those benefits do not justify its broad retry refactor and associated documentation churn.
risks_a: Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of the required FilesService.Add path.
The global replayableReader machinery changes streaming, memory use, read timing, and potentially reader-closing behavior for unrelated APIs.
Its new behavior is applied whenever WithNoRetry is absent, even when the configured policy would not retry that request.
risks_b: Upload delegates to private add rather than the contractually required public Add method.
Add now eagerly consumes and buffers all custom bodies, changing its prior streaming behavior.

Upload has no visible empty-filename or nil-content validation before multipartbody.NewFile; nil handling may depend unsafely on the helper. Tests for both validation and source-reader errors are missing.
